problems.title: When a trie?

options: Autocomplete: all words starting with a typed prefix
Is this exact word in a fixed set? (single lookups)
Find many dictionary words in a letter grid
Maximum XOR of two numbers in an array

problems.solution: Exact lookups only need a hash set. Max XOR uses a binary trie.

problems.title: Node count
problems.statement: Insert app, apple, apply, apt, bat, bath into a trie (count the root as a node).

parts.prompt: Nodes marked as a word end?

hints: Count the distinct prefixes, plus the root.
problems.solution: The distinct prefixes are a, ap, app, appl, apple, apply, apt, b, ba, bat, bath: 11, plus the root gives 12. There are 6 end markers, one per word ("app" is both a word and a prefix).

problems.title: search vs starts_with
problems.solution: The walk succeeds for "app", but its node isn't marked as a word end.

problems.title: Cost

parts.prompt: How does this depend on the number of stored words?

problems.solution: O(|p|), independent of the dictionary size. That independence is the point of a trie.

problems.title: Memory
problems.statement: 10⁴ words of average length 10, with no shared prefixes in the worst case, stored as array-of-26 nodes with 8-byte pointers.
problems.solution: About 10⁵ nodes × 208 bytes ≈ 20.8 MB. That's fine here, but it explains why dict or compressed (radix) nodes exist.

problems.title: Wildcards
problems.statement: Add-and-search-word with '.' matching any one letter, words of length ≤ 25, at most 2 dots per query.

parts.prompt: Worst-case branches explored for two dots (lowercase letters)?

problems.solution: Each dot multiplies the frontier by at most 26, so 676 paths for two dots. That's the reason for the small-dots constraint.

problems.title: Max XOR
problems.statement: A binary trie over the 5-bit numbers [3, 10, 5, 25, 2, 8]. What is the maximum XOR of a pair?

parts.prompt: Per query, at each bit the walk…
options: prefers the child with the opposite bit

problems.solution: 5 ^ 25 = 28. Greedy from the top bit: an opposite bit there beats anything the lower bits can contribute.

problems.title: Word Search II reasoning

parts.prompt: What makes the per-word DFS slow?
options: Shared prefixes are explored again for every word
The grid is too large to read

parts.prompt: Which refinements help the trie solution?
options: Store the word at its end node
Prune trie branches that become empty

problems.solution: One DFS per cell walks the trie; storing words avoids string building; removing found words and pruning dead branches stop repeated work.
